title: Incremental soft-credit reconciliation with finalization waves for at-least-once ingest
creator: Aisha Raman
description:
Problem: We observe transient duplicate charges when clients retry requests (network timeouts, SDK retries, mobile flakiness). Current hedging uses aggressive dedupe tokens and long-lived leases which increase latency and coordination complexity at the edge.

Proposal: Implement an "incremental soft-credit + finalization waves" protocol. Incoming requests get a provisional soft credit (cheap, idempotent) recorded immediately. The system continues serving at least-once. A separate finalization wave reconciler will periodically (by customer, region, and route) collapse provisional credits into final charges using deterministic lineage signals and probabilistic suppression heuristics. This reduces tail latency on ingest, tolerates edge clock skew and network partitions, and keeps reconciliation work asynchronous in a bounded window.

Key concepts:
- provisional_credit record: lightweight entry that attributes tokens/units to (customer, route, provisional_id, event_ts, hint_tags).
- finalization_id (wave id): reconciler groups provisional records into waves using epoch windows (e.g., 30s/5m depending on customer tier).
- lineage hints: client-provided request_fingerprint + sequence_hint + optional parent_id to increase dedupe confidence.
- suppression heuristics: (1) exact fingerprint match => immediate suppression, (2) high similarity + small time delta => probabilistic merge, (3) manual override for customer disputes.
- rollback / charge-back path: reconciler emits exceptions for suspected duplicates; Accounting jobs create negative correction entries with audit trail.

Why different from prior approaches: instead of long-grained global leases or synchronous reservation commits, this design shifts to fast local soft credits and a delayed deterministic consolidation step that can be scaled independently and tuned per-customer to trade latency for correctness and operational cost.
acceptance_criteria: API: New provisional_credit flag accepted on ingest; default behavior unchanged for clients without hints
No increase in 99th-percentile ingest latency across representative routes (target: <= +5ms median, <= +15ms 99p)
End-to-end unit test coverage for provisional -> finalization state transitions and charge-back path
Reconciler job runs with configurable window; end-state produced is idempotent and converges within the wave window
Billing numbers for a test tenant show <= 0.1% variance vs ground-truth after 48h reconciliation in synthetic retry scenarios
Operational dashboards: provisional counts, reconciliation lag histogram, suppressed-duplicates-rate, charge-backs emitted

notes: Data model: provisional_credit rows live in the lightweight accounting store (time-series-append) with TTL of 14 days. Final charges written to canonical ledger only by reconciler to ensure single-writer semantics per finalization_id.
Backfill: for existing provisional-like rows from previous experiments, run a one-off consolidation job that marks them as historical; do not re-charge customers during migration window.
Testing: create synthetic clients that exercise at-least-once profiles (duplicate bursts, sequenced retries, clock-skewed duplicates). Verify reconciler merges correctly under load.

Rollout plan: (1) internal tenants only, (2) opt-in customers with high retry rates, (3) gradual global enable by traffic weight. Monitor suppressed-duplicates-rate and customer support tickets closely.

Edge considerations: avoid large per-request metadata; default fingerprint = sha256(request_body | route | customer_id) produced in SDKs; server will accept absent fingerprint but treat with lower dedupe confidence.
Observability: emit reconciliation wave metadata (wave_id, start_ts, end_ts, covered_count, merged_count, corrections_emitted) to tracing and billing metrics.
SLA: reconciler can be delayed up to configured max_lag (default 5 minutes for free tier, 30s for enterprise). Provide alerting when lag > max_lag for >5% customers.
Open question: decide suppression threshold tuning that minimizes false-positives while keeping cost of reconciliation low. Experiment with logistic-regression model on historical retries.
Compliance: finalization records must include audit signature and hash of contributing provisional ids to satisfy finance audit requirements.
